Passed on the fake backend by `python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/robots/vimalabs__vimabench --backend fake`; evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. Model-authored by deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 (run wC-046) and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by null); no human review, hardware attachment or hardware run is claimed, and the sim backend was not run. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's GymnasiumDriver/family-config shape cannot express this upstream. A GymnasiumDriver derives the contract from `gymnasium.make(env_id)` and its spaces; VIMA-Bench is built by its own factory `vima_bench.make(task_name=...)` (vima_bench/__init__.py:14-42) and the clone registers no Gymnasium id (no gym.register call exists in it). This package is a direct Driver over the confirmed entry symbol vima_bench.env.base:VIMAEnvBase. The sim backend names the clone's own factory `vima_bench:make`; it needs pybullet, gym==0.21.0 and the clone's assets (requirements.txt:1-2) and was not run. The bound classes are cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1. The action-space limits are the upstream Box bounds [0.25, -0.5]..[0.75, 0.50] for both positions and -1.0..1.0 for both four-element rotations (vima_bench/env/base.py:181-196); the step ticks bounds (1..10000) and the reset/seed seed minimum (0) are inherited from the catalogue class schemas, not restated as driver Limits. The package fake (fake.py) is a pure Python kinematic stand-in: it moves one placeholder object to the place position, always returns reward 0 and done=success, and never uses PyBullet, the UR5, the assets, contact dynamics or a task's success/failure logic. Its start positions, target, success radius, prompt text, ee value and image arrays are test data marked `# placeholder`; they are not facts, limits or citations. The fake returns smaller arrays than the device: 3 x 2 x 2 rgb and 2 x 2 segm per view, while the real task defaults are 3 x 128 x 256 rgb and 128 x 256 segm per view (vima_bench/tasks/task_suite/base.py:67); the real size is named here and in the fidelity gaps. The fake was never compared with the upstream PyBullet environment. The upstream seed does not control every draw: some task code uses Python's global random (vima_bench/tasks/task_suite/base.py:560) and numpy's global generator (:599), so the fidelity kind seeded describes the documented seed control and the fake, and the gaps state that the upstream path is not fully reproducible from the seed alone. NOT COVERED: rendering (cap.world.render.v1 needs an artifact store); the prompt_assets images (the prompt string is exposed in the info read and the reset output has the observation and seed); the depth modality (the clone rejects it at vima_bench/env/base.py:67); snapshot/restore (VIMAEnvBase exposes no get_state/set_state); and the PyBullet contact, UR5, asset and task semantics, which only the sim backend would exercise. The fidelity timestep_ms 4.166666666666667 is the PyBullet physics step 1/hz with the constructor default hz=240 (vima_bench/env/base.py:36 and :131); one cap.world.step.v1 tick is one VIMAEnvBase.step primitive, which integrates a variable number of those physics steps until the objects are static (vima_bench/env/base.py:391-433), so ticks x timestep_ms is not the duration of one primitive and the gaps say the control period is not fixed. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings were reported, and the last gate run had no warnings at all. Only catalogue classes are bound, so there are no catalogue requests and no extension ids. gate.digest is the digest line the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
